title: AGS-GNN: Attribute-guided Sampling for Graph Neural Network

problem.claim: GNNs face challenges on heterophilic graphs, where state-of-the-art methods use full neighborhoods and therefore do not scale to large graphs or support inductive use.

gap.claim: Existing heterophilic GNN approaches do not provide scalable neighborhood sampling that adapts to both homophilic and heterophilic structure.

contributions.claim: AGS-GNN uses dual-channel feature-similarity and feature-diversity sampling to select adaptive neighbor subsets for homophilic and heterophilic neighborhoods.
The approach uses submodularity for diverse neighborhood sampling and pre-computes sampling distributions in parallel for scalability.
AGS-GNN can be incorporated into existing GNN models that use node or graph sampling.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present AGS-GNN as a novel attribute-guided sampling algorithm and identify submodularity for diverse neighborhood sampling as a novel contribution in this context.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On a dataset of 35 small and large homophilic and heterophilic graphs, the authors report that AGS-GNN outperforms state-of-the-art approaches.
The authors report test accuracy comparable to the best-performing heterophilic GNNs, including methods that use the entire graph for node classification.
The authors report faster convergence than randomly sampled neighborhood methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper proposes AGS-GNN, an attribute-guided sampling algorithm for GNNs.
It targets the differing neighborhood structures of homophilic and heterophilic graphs and the scalability and inductive limitations of existing heterophilic GNNs.
AGS-GNN combines feature-similarity and feature-diversity sampling, uses submodularity for diverse sampling, and pre-computes sampling distributions in parallel.
The authors evaluate AGS-GNN on 35 small and large homophilic and heterophilic graphs.
The authors report competitive accuracy, faster convergence than random neighborhood sampling, and compatibility with existing sampled GNN models.

source_observation.claim: Sampling based on both feature similarity and feature diversity is designed to adapt to homophilic and heterophilic neighborhoods.

interpretation.claim: A sampling strategy may need to preserve both local agreement and informative diversity when graph neighborhood structure varies.

application.claim: For graph learning systems spanning different structural regimes, consider combining similar-neighbor and diverse-neighbor selection.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported graph datasets or tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact sampling algorithm, model architecture, or hyperparameters.
The abstract does not provide per-dataset results, statistical comparisons, or computational cost measurements.
The abstract does not independently verify the reported superiority, accuracy, scalability, or convergence claims.
